derivedFrom: the decision that a suspect name's retries are bounded and a name whose retries are spent stays suspect and named on the run page until another action lands on it, not a run. A name whose refetch fails on the night an action lands on it is marked with no retries counted; it is asked for again on each of the next five nights and each failure counts one more; on the nights after the fifth it is not asked for and is named as spent; a night an action lands on it again asks for it and starts the count at none, and the night after asks again. So the per-name requests the check makes for the name are one on each of the first six nights, none on the next two, and one on each of the last two, and one action costs at most six. The first night is the session AAPL's captured action is dated; the nights after it are the sessions the exchange traded, read off the closure table at test time rather than written here, and the action that lands again is the test's own on the ninth.
